title: Getting started: a new project, start to finish
description: A coolant system added to the Desktop CNC Mill: a project filed under the mill, its first requirement, the link to the mill requirement it refines, then the test, the plan and a baseline.

steps.say: This is OpenV. Each product, and each part of a product, is a project. Here is the Desktop CNC Mill: fifteen projects, from the whole machine down to its motors and its software.
A project opens on its overview: what the product is for, who it is for, the limits it has to work within, and how you will know it has succeeded.
In this video we add something the mill does not have yet: a coolant system, with a project of its own under the mill.
Create a project, and file it under the mill. Its requirements can then refine the mill's, and its test results will count toward them.

do: The pump, tank, nozzles and returns that cool the cut and carry the chips away.
steps.say: A line of description, and the project is ready.
Its first requirement. Each one is an artifact: a requirement, a user need, a design item, a hazard or a test case.

do: The coolant system shall return all coolant to the tank and shall leak none outside the enclosure at a flow of 2 litres a minute.
steps.say: Give it a title and say what the system shall do, in a way somebody could test.
It gets a reference that never changes, R E Q one, and a wording score. One hundred: it uses shall, names a number, and has nothing vague in it.

do: input[placeholder='Type to search by title or UID...']
steps.say: Now link it to the mill requirement it refines. The search reaches the parent project, so pick the mill's requirement that keeps chips and coolant inside.

do: text=Chips and coolant stay inside >> nth=-1
steps.say: Add the link and save. The trace now shows one link up, to the mill's requirement number twelve, in the Desktop CNC Mill project.
And in the mill's project, that requirement now lists the coolant system's among the requirements that refine it. When the coolant tests pass, the mill's requirement will count them.
The next steps are the same in every project. Add a test case that verifies the requirement, and record its results in a test run on the V and V page.
Plan the work on the Gantt: tasks, milestones and the reviews they lead to, and link a task to the mill's plan where the mill is waiting for it.
And when the requirements are agreed, capture a baseline, so you can show later exactly what was agreed and what has changed since.
That is the whole loop: define, link, verify, plan and baseline. The short videos on the demos page go into each one in turn.
